newsitem.title: UK: EMI gains again on bid report in newspaper.
newsitem.headline: EMI gains again on bid report in newspaper.

text.p: Shares in leading British music publisher EMI Group Plc pushed ahead again on Wednesday morning after a newspaper report that other companies were lining up a bid, dealers said.
EMI shares were up 25 pence at 1225p by 0950 GMT on volume of 260,000, outperforming a strong FTSE-100 which was up 40 points at 4,386.
The Financial Times newspaper said speculation continued that Seagram Co Ltd may launch a bid attempt. The FT said Walt Disney, News Corp and Viacom were also said to be eyeing a bid.

EMI said on Tuesday it had no comment on reports alleging it had been in failed merger talks with Seagram, the Canadian drinks and entertainment group. A spokesman for EMI said it was the company's closed period and it could not comment.
Neither company has previously made any mention of being in merger talks. Analysts said EMI has long been regarded as a takeover target and Seagram was seen as the likeliest bidder.
Bid speculation for EMI intensified last summer when the group demerged from its former parent Thorn EMI which split up its music and rental businesses.
